messages:
arya: Heads-up — CI is red for the flash-attn packaging job on manylinux wheel build. Lots of symbol errors and then a perf regression on the nightly perf-runner after the wheel was deployed. link: https://buildkite.com/redwood/flash-pack/builds/9876 :frowning:
ci-bot: buildkite #9876 — manylinux wheel: FAILED (link errors) — see artifacts/logs/build.log
ben: seeing GLIBCXX_3.4.30 undefined symbol in the linker output. packaging image uses gcc-11 on manylinux2014, while our internal nodes use gcc-12. That mismatch can produce subtle ABI drops for template instantiations in the fused kernels.
marta: also saw a runtime crash on the perf cluster: CUDA kernel launch failure: invalid device function. Seems like the kernel variant chosen at runtime doesn't match what was actually built into the wheel.
arya: repro steps I ran locally: build wheel in manylinux2014 container + install on an amber GPU node (compute 8.6). Then run the fused attention smoke: `python -m tests.attn_smoke --variant fused --seq 2048 --batch 4` => kernel launch fails.
tomas: quick note: our pack CI sets CMAKE_C_FLAGS="-O0 -g" for easier debugging but the released artifact ended up with those flags baked in because the release job accidentally re-used the debug container. That explains the extra host checks in the kernel and the huge memcpy overhead in traces.
sarah: profiling data (perf + Nsight): p50 roughly same, but p99 jumped from 120ms to 320ms on chat workload after this wheel. Flamegraph shows ~30% of time in device->host memcpy around KV cache eviction logic.
ben: why would memcpy increase? Are we serializing KV to host on kernel mismatch?
marta: yes — when kernel-variant compatibility check fails at runtime, we fall back to the slow-path that materializes KV on host and does per-token barrier + memcpy. That's the KV thrash. It used to be rare, now it's common because the runtime's kernel selector reads the compiled feature flags embedded in the wheel and they didn't match the node capabilities.
arya: root causes summary: (1) manylinux image toolchain mismatch -> ABI/symbol fallout, (2) release job reused debug build container -> debug flags in artifacts, (3) runtime kernel selector picks wrong variant when compiled metadata mismatches, causing KV host fallback and p99 spike.
ben: quick fixes I pushed in branch `fix/pack-ci-gcc12` — updated the build image to gcc-12, pinned libstdc++ packaging, and added a post-build check script that calls `readelf -Ws` to ensure GLIBCXX symbols are present. Also separated the debug vs release containers. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/421
sarah: long-term we should avoid relying purely on compile-time metadata. Suggest adding a runtime feature-hash check + deterministic fallback ordering: prefer in-GPU variants, but if binary feature mismatch -> try a lightly-recompiled or compatible kernel bundle before doing host fallback.
tomas: agreed. Proposed incremental plan: 1) revert the bad wheel in the hosted fleet (rollback job queued), 2) add CI gate that runs a tiny smoke on a GPU emulator (or CI GPU runners) to validate kernel launch, 3) patch runtime to detect and prefer compatible kernel groups, 4) change batching heuristic temporarily to cap batch*seq so we don't hit worst-case KV eviction pattern while patching.
marta: for point (3) I sketched an approach: store a small per-kernel capability vector (compute capability, sm arch, compiled compute flags, kernel ABI version). At startup, the runtime computes compatibility score and maps requested kernel->actual loaded kernel. If score < threshold, do a fast JIT build of a compatible shim (cuda kernel compile) or fall back to the verified variant.
arya: example check snippet I added to the CI smoke (`pack_checks.sh`):
```
# verify required GLIBCXX symbols are present
python - <<PY
import subprocess,sys
out = subprocess.check_output(["readelf","-Ws", "./build/libredwood_attn.so"]).decode()
if 'GLIBCXX_3.4.30' not in out:
    print('missing symbol')
    sys.exit(1)
print('ok')
PY
```
ben: also removed `-ffast-math` from fused kernel builds. That flag allowed some algebraic reordering which broke numeric assumptions in the paged attention path; keeping strict IEEE seems to stabilize convergence and avoids some kernel specialization mismatches.
sarah: for KV cache mitigation: add a soft LRU and increase in-GPU KV budget by 10% when we detect repeated kernel-switch-induced evictions. Helps avoid p99 blasts in the short term.
tomas: CI changes to land: - use gcc-12 manylinux2022 image, - split debug/release workflows, - add `pack_checks.sh` as a required step, - smoke run on a small GPU runner (NVIDIA A100 emulator or a small fleet runner).
marta: I also added a tiny perf test that runs a 1-minute chat QPS profile and collects torch.cuda.synchronize timings. It now runs in CI nightly and will alert if p99 > 200ms.
arya: can someone approve the rollback + the PR? Need to get the hosted fleet back to green before EOD.
ben: approving PR, triggering rollback now.
ci-bot: buildkite #9880 — rollback wheel deployed to hosted fleet — SUCCESS
sarah: after rollback p99 is back to ~130ms in the canary region. We'll continue with the runtime compatibility patch and the packaging fixes.
arya: thanks all. Follow-up items: assign runtime selector work to @marta, CI packaging to @ben, KV fallback/LRU to @sarah. I'll create follow-up tickets and link to this thread.
ben: created tickets: RNW-1041 (packaging), RNW-1042 (runtime-selector), RNW-1043 (kv-lru).
marta: logging action: adding a compact regression note to the weekly perf changelog so product knows why the regressions happened. :white_check_mark:
